messages:
maya: Heads-up - prototype for a different quota & routing approach for embeds: 'unitization'. TL;DR: convert mixed-dim payloads into canonical units so routing and quotas are predictable.

jen: curious, can you sketch the unit definition? sounds like a billing trick at first glance.

maya: not billing-only. unit = max(dim_count, ceil(bytes / 256)). Essentially a small, medium, large unit model so router can pick compact vs wide-serving pools.

sam: so a 64-dim @ 4KB payload -> unit = max(64, ceil(4096/256)=16) => 64, still small. but 4096 bytes could be many vectors?

maya: right. it's conservative for dims. The idea is if dims > 512 we prefer 'wide' shards, else compact models. It aligns routing with runtime memory footprints.

alex: how does this affect batching? we currently batch by tokens/dim compatibility. If unitizes, do we sum units to check batch cap?

maya: yes, batch cap becomes units_per_batch (e.g., 1024 units). So a request with 512-dim x 3 vectors = 1536 units -> split. That's simpler than current mixed-dim heuristics.

jen: what about existing console UX and telemetry? ops teams want visibility into which units caused slow requests.

maya: propose console additions: per-route "unit histogram" (sampled), and a new telemetry event embed.unit_route_decision with fields: model_variant, total_units, split_reason.

ops-bot: Notice: creating new telemetry event will increase cardinality. Recommend sampling 1/100 for unit-level payloads.

tariq: on quotas - do we map units back to credit model? e.g., 1 unit = 1 embed-unit credit? we need to be clear for customers.

maya: yes, documentation will show credits = units * price_per_unit(model). For Dedicated we allow locking unit price per contract.

sam: edge: extremely wide but tiny byte size (e.g., sparse encodings). unit = dims dominates, so route to wide. Good. But what about many short vectors (dim 32) huge payload due to metadata?

maya: strip out metadata for unit calc (only vector bytes considered). We already do this in the SDK, but server should sanity-check.

jen: SDK changes needed. We should add preflight endpoint to return estimated units and suggested route. That helps clients fast-fail big payloads and show console hints.

alex: preflight ok but backward compat: if older SDKs don't call preflight they'll get 413s or splits. Need graceful fallback.

maya: plan: server will accept mixed requests but tag oversize splits in response: 207-like wrapper with per-item routing/split info and a top-level header X-Embed-Unit-Estimate. Old SDKs see header and can surface message.

tariq: telemetry for errors? add event embed.split_applied with reason=cross_unit_limit or max_batch. We also need rollout metrics: ratio of requests requiring split per route.

jen: console: add a routing heatmap by unit-size bucket (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024). Operator can toggle canary flag for new routing in Console -> Routes -> Advanced.

ops-bot: Deploy checklist: feature-flagged routing, preflight opt-in, 0.1% rollout, backfill telemetry, billing mapping validated in staging.

sam: what about quota enforcement semantics? If account hits unit quota mid-batch, do we partial-fulfill some vectors?

maya: policy options: (A) fast-fail entire request, (B) partial success with 206 per-item and charge for returned units, (C) enqueue for Dedicated burst. My vote B (partial). Less surprising for embeddings use-cases.

tariq: partial can be messy for clients expecting fixed order. Must include mapping ids -> result index in 206. Also need a console alert when partials spike.

jen: UX: console tooltip for routes: "Units: estimate model cost + routing affinity. Use preflight for accurate estimates." Keep wording simple.

alex: rollout timeline? we need runtime + console + SDK + billing hooks. I'd say 4 weeks with canary first 10% tenants on low-traffic routes.

maya: proposed schedule: week1 runtime + feature flag, week2 console + telemetry, week3 SDK preflight + docs, week4 canary + billing audit. Rapid revert plan included.

sam: tests: simulation harness for mixed-dim traffic, fuzz payloads w/ metadata bloat, e2e billing check.

jen: one more: rate-limiter interplay. If routing moves requests to compact pool, rate limits per-pool differ. Need cross-pool quota checks to avoid bypassing tenant-level limits.

maya: agreed. router will check tenant_global_units_quota before routing and attach quota_reservation in header. If reservation fails, return 429.

ops-bot: Action items created: #1 maya implement unitization proto; #2 alex add console buckets; #3 jen coordinate SDK preflight; #4 tariq wire telemetry and quota reservation.

maya: thanks all. I'll post a short RFC in #eng-platform with numbers and example responses. Ping me if you want to be on the canary list. :rocket:
